name: deepchem/deepchem
what_it_is: DeepChem is an open-source Python library that provides deep learning models, featurizers, datasets, and benchmarks for drug discovery, quantum chemistry, materials science, and computational biology. It wraps TensorFlow, PyTorch, and JAX backends under a unified API, with MoleculeNet as its curated benchmark suite.
components: deepchem.models — model zoo (GCN, GAT, MPNN, AttentiveFP, ChemBERTa, MolFormer, GROVER, FermiNet, DTNN, GAN, MolGAN, seq2seq, sklearn wrappers, and more)

deepchem.feat — featurizer library (circular fingerprints, Coulomb matrices, graph convolution, RDKit descriptors, Mordred, MACCS keys, PubChem fingerprints, image featurizers, material featurizers, sequence featurizers)
deepchem.molnet — MoleculeNet dataset loaders (Tox21, HIV, BACE, BBBP, ClinTox, MUV, PCBA, QM7/8/9, PDBbind, ZINC15, ChEMBL, and others)
deepchem.dock — molecular docking module (pose generation, pose scoring, binding pocket detection)
measurement: Model training and evaluation metrics (accuracy, AUC-ROC, RMSE, MAE, R2, etc.) via deepchem.metrics
Weights & Biases integration for tracking training and evaluation metrics
configuration: Choice of deep learning backend: TensorFlow, PyTorch, or JAX (installed as optional extras)
GPU vs CPU execution (CUDA required for GPU)
Dataset splitting strategy (random, scaffold, stratified, etc.) via deepchem.splits
modes: Library mode — imported as a Python package in scripts or notebooks
Docker image — deepchemio/deepchem:latest (nightly, GPU-enabled) or versioned tag images
Google Colab tutorials — pre-built Jupyter notebooks for interactive use
constraints: Python 3.7-3.10 only; Python 3.11+ not officially supported per README
No no-code or GUI interface; all usage requires Python scripting or notebooks
Docking module depends on external third-party docking engines for pose generation; DeepChem only wraps them
Soft dependencies (TensorFlow, PyTorch, JAX, RDKit, etc.) must be installed separately per use case; a plain pip install gives only the minimal core
Docker images are single-container; no orchestrated multi-service compose configuration is provided
notable_absences: No REST API or web service interface
No built-in experiment database or model registry
No native support for protein structure prediction (e.g., AlphaFold-style folding)
No visual/GUI molecular editor or viewer
